knowledge:
- key_parameters: o=The first argument to mgsa(), representing the observed active genes (study set) as a character vector ;; sets=The second argument to mgsa(), representing the gene sets (can be a list, MgsaSets, or MgsaGoSets object) ;; alpha=The false positive rate parameter (probability of an inactive gene to be observed) ;; beta=The false negative rate parameter (probability of an active gene to not be observed) ;; p=The prior probability for any set to be active
- alternatives: Classical gene set enrichment analysis (which analyzes each set in isolation and often yields redundant, overlapping results)
- when_to_use: When performing gene set enrichment analysis on a list of active genes (e.g., differentially expressed genes or screen hits) and wanting to account for gene set overlaps to obtain a concise, non-redundant list of active pathways
- pitfalls: Running mgsa() repeatedly on the same gene sets with different observations can be slow; users should pre-index the sets by creating an MgsaSets object using new("MgsaSets", sets=...) to speed up computations. Also, readGAF() requires the GO.db and RSQLite packages to be installed.

workflows.name: mgsa_gene_ontology
workflows.intent: Perform model-based gene set enrichment analysis using Gene Ontology annotations loaded from a GAF file.
workflows.stages: 1. Load GO annotations from a GAF file using readGAF ;; 2. Run MGSA using mgsa ;; 3. Plot the posterior probabilities using plot ;; 4. Extract and filter results using setsResults and subset
workflows.code:
library(mgsa)
readGAF(
	system.file(
		"example_files/gene_association_head.sgd",
		package="mgsa"
	)
)
set.seed(0)
fit = mgsa(example_o, example_go)
fit
plot(fit)
res = setsResults(fit)
subset(res, estimate > 0.5)

workflows.name: mgsa_custom_sets
workflows.intent: Perform model-based gene set enrichment analysis using custom-defined gene sets.
workflows.stages: 1. Run MGSA directly with a list of custom sets, or pre-index them by creating an MgsaSets object ;; 2. Run MGSA using mgsa with the pre-indexed sets for multiple observations
workflows.code:
mgsa( c("A", "B"), list(set1=LETTERS[1:3], set2=LETTERS[2:5]) ) 
myset = new( "MgsaSets", sets=list(set1=LETTERS[1:3], set2=LETTERS[2:5]) )
mgsa(c("A", "B"), myset)
mgsa(c("B", "C"), myset)
